summary: Grandson of Bull Smith and great-grandfather of Judge J. Lawrence Smith; John's 1st cousin 10 times removed.
bio:
Ebenezer Smith was born on 20 February 1712, the son of Richard Smith 2d and a grandson of Bull Smith. The family record of his father's children gives the event in the words of the time: 'Ebenezer Smith Sun of Richard Smith was borne ye twentieth Day of February about 2 o'clock in the afternoone In the yeare of our Lord 1712.'

He married Anna, a daughter of Job Smith 2d, and their children were Richard 4th, Phineas, who was lost at sea, Temperance, who married Jonas Platt, Hannah, who married Joshua Smith 1st, and Anna, who married Rev. William Dodge. His will, dated 25 July 1747 and proved in January 1748, left £100 to each of his daughters Temperance, Anna and Hannah when they came of age. His widow Anna married Zephaniah Platt. His homestead passed down the male line and was still held by his descendants in 1898 as the 'Dick 'Nezer Place'.

Through his son Richard 4th he was the great-grandfather of Judge J. Lawrence Smith. He is John's 1st cousin 10 times removed through Bull Smith. He was once thought a possible father of the Temperance Tuttle in John's own line, but that has been ruled out.

researchNotes:
Will dated 25 Jul 1747, proved 7 Jan 1747 O.S. (i.e., 1748 N.S.), leaving £100 each to 'my daughters Temperance Anna and Hannah' when 21 (Pelletreau p. 46). His homestead passed down his male line and was still held in 1898 as the 'Dick 'Nezer Place' (p. 46 note). His widow Anna married Zephaniah Platt.

His birth is in the verbatim family record of Richard Smith 2d's children printed by Pelletreau ([R4-S1]): 'Ebenezer Smith Sun of Richard Smith was borne ye twentieth Day of February about 2 o'clock in the afternoone In the yeare of our Lord 1712.' Children with Anna (daughter of Job 2d): Richard 4th, Phineas (lost at sea), Temperance (Mrs Jonas Platt), Hannah (Mrs Joshua Smith 1st) and Anna (Mrs Rev. William Dodge). Through Richard 4th he is the great-grandfather of Judge J. Lawrence Smith.
